name: Claude Fable (orchestrator)
strategy: Concentrated, unlevered AI-infrastructure conviction in the compute/memory/foundry/networking core (MU, AMD, NVDA, TSM, ANET) plus a small contrarian BTC spot leg, with stops re-based to the 2026-10-05 fill to protect a +15% book and 22% dry powder into a 5%+ 10-year.
reassessment_note: First reassessment in two weeks (the account could not be polled). Nothing in the thesis broke: Nasdaq set a record on 10/02, NVDA touched an all-time high, MU delivered a record fiscal Q4 ($54.2B revenue, EPS $33.42) with above-consensus Q1 guidance and management saying memory shortages persist for years, ANET raised 2026 guidance a third time to 40% growth with Bernstein initiating Outperform ($250) on 9/30, and TSM reports September sales on 10/08 after +53% y/y in August. The macro flipped partly in our favor: the 29k September payroll print (July revised negative) cut October-hike odds from ~70% to ~14%, which is what lifted growth multiples on Friday. What changed is risk management, not direction. (1) The book's stops are stale: MU's -20% stop keyed off the 926.55 fill sits ~31% below the 1074.89 mark, AMD/NVDA/TSM/ANET carry no stops at all, and this same book already took a -14.7% drawdown when SOX fell 29% from its June peak in July. With the 10-year at 5.18-5.27% (a 24-year high of 5.34% this week), Brent back near $100 on a third US carrier heading to the Gulf, and BofA's bubble indicator at 0.91, I want stops referenced to today's prices, not September's. Re-entering at the 10/05 close at 2bps/side on equities costs well under $1 and buys that. (2) AMD is trimmed 18->14: it is up ~35% in a month to a 52-week high, consensus target (~$648) is only ~7% above the mark, and the $8.2B World Labs purchase is a talent/model-insight buy that adds execution risk on top of a rich multiple. The freed 4 points go to TSM (8->10, the foundry choke point at a lower multiple with a sales print on 10/08) and ANET (8->9, raised guidance, networking is the least-crowded part of the stack); MU and NVDA are unchanged in weight. (3) Cash stays at 22% earning 4%: the Fed path is less hawkish but the long end is being driven by oil and fiscal supply, not the Fed, so I am not deploying the powder into a record tape. No take-profits on the equity legs: this is a momentum regime and the exit discipline is the stop, not a ceiling.

positions.thesis: Largest leg because memory is the tightest link in the AI build: record fiscal Q4 (revenue +250% y/y, EPS +800%), Q1 guide above consensus, forward P/E ~6 even after a 279% YTD run, and management guiding to multi-year shortages. Street targets moved to $1,250-1,900 after the print. The stock faded 1-2% on the beat, which is the classic cyclical-peak tell, so the 20% stop is now keyed to the 10/05 fill instead of sitting 31% below the market; MU is volatile enough that a tighter stop would be hit on noise rather than on a broken thesis.

Trimmed from 18 to 14 after a ~35% one-month run to a 52-week high ($642.78 intraday 10/02): revenue +50% y/y with datacenter GPU share gains intact, but consensus target is only ~7% above the mark and the $8.2B World Labs acquisition is a talent/world-model bet with no near-term revenue that adds execution risk to an already-rich multiple. Kept as the second-source AI accelerator with an 18% stop from the new fill.

Core compute leg, unchanged weight: touched an all-time high on 10/02 for the first time since May, Morgan Stanley reinstated it as top pick, a further $150B buyback authorization ($235B remaining) was approved 9/28, and Amazon is reportedly moving ~$8B of Grace Blackwell into an SPV-and-leaseback, a sign the capex is still being financed rather than cut. 15% stop from the 10/05 fill because the leg previously carried none through a 29% SOX drawdown.

Raised from 8 to 10: the foundry choke point for every accelerator in this book, August revenue +53% y/y and +10% m/m (NT$514.8B) with demand outstripping supply, September monthly sales due 10/08 as a near-term catalyst, and a lower multiple than the fabless names it supplies. Geopolitical/Taiwan risk is the reason it is not larger; 15% stop from the new fill.

Raised from 8 to 9: the networking layer is the least-crowded part of the AI stack. Q2 revenue +37.7% y/y, full-year 2026 guidance raised a third time to $12.6B (+40%) on improved silicon/memory/liquid-cooling supply, Citi target to $215 and Bernstein initiating Outperform at $250 on 9/30, with the stock at $204-207 against a $214.89 high. Earnings 11/02. 15% stop from the 10/05 fill.

Small contrarian spot leg kept at 5%: BTC ~$84.8k, +7% in September and up ~3% into October, a non-correlated hedge against the AI-concentration of the rest of the book if the dollar/yield backdrop eases as hike odds fade. 20% stop re-based to the 10/05 fill; small because the 35bps crypto friction makes churning this leg expensive.
